title: MapReduce & the Shuffle
summary: How MapReduce turns a map function and a reduce function into a parallel job, why the shuffle is the expensive part, how a stable partitioner and sorted reducer input make it work, and when a combiner can shrink it.
takeaways: Map runs independently on each input split. Reduce runs once per key, after the shuffle has gathered all of that key's values on one machine.
The partitioner decides which reducer owns a key. It must give the same answer on every machine, so use a stable hash like CRC32, never Python's salted hash().
Each reducer receives its keys sorted, which makes grouping a streaming merge and the output ordered within each partition.
A combiner pre-aggregates inside a map task to cut shuffle volume. It's only safe for associative, commutative operations, so compute a mean by carrying (sum, count).

steps.label: Split
steps.detail: Cut the input into M splits. Each one becomes an independent map task.

steps.label: Map
steps.detail: Call map(record) for every record and collect the intermediate (key, value) pairs.

steps.label: Combine
steps.detail: Optionally pre-reduce each map task's output per key, so fewer pairs leave the machine.

steps.label: Partition + shuffle
steps.detail: Send each pair to reducer crc32(key) mod R. This is the all-to-all network transfer.

steps.label: Sort + reduce
steps.detail: Each reducer sorts its pairs by key and calls reduce(key, values) once per key.

terms.definition: A contiguous chunk of the input processed by one map task. Splits let M machines read in parallel.
The phase that moves every intermediate pair from the map task that produced it to the reducer that owns its key. It's usually the most expensive part of a job.
The function from key to reducer index, by default hash(key) mod R. It must be deterministic across processes and machines.
A mini-reduce run on each map task's output before the shuffle. It's valid only when the operation is associative and commutative.
A task that runs much longer than its peers, so the whole stage has to wait for it.
